text: Okay, okay, all right, why'd you break the heart? Uh, there was a previous comment about accountability, which I found to be kind of a red flag, not because I don't take accountability, but it usually means that you are looking for the other person's issues versus also taking accountability. What the hell did she even say? But it seems like if you ever want to know who you're dealing with, just say the word accountability and watch the reaction. But basically, she popped the guy's balloon heart because he mentioned earlier that the woman should have accountability? You can't make this up, man. And if I understood her, it is a red flag because it is looking for the other person's issues? So in other words, isn't she saying that she doesn't like the idea that her behavior might ever be questioned? So this is one of the problems of modern dating. A man says, I want mutual accountability, and the interpretation becomes, you are controlling, you are blaming, you are focused on my flaws. Translation, she wants the power to judge, reject, and disqualify, but she doesn't want the mirror to be turned around. Basically, relationships require both adults to be taking responsibility for their actions. If the simple idea of accountability triggers someone, that's not a cute personality quirk. That's a warning sign. Because when something goes wrong later, guess who will always be the victim and who will always be the problem? So yeah, man, pay attention. If the word accountability makes her uncomfortable, defensive, or weirdly philosophical, that balloon should be popped from your side, not hers.
